competition.title: Business Model Teardown Challenge
competition.details:
Business Model Teardown Challenge

Decode. Disrupt. Rebuild.

Powered by Unstop | Organized by E-Cell, Great Lakes Institute of Management

About the Competition

What if you could take apart the business model of a billion-dollar company, identify what makes it successful, find where it can break, and then rebuild it for the future?

Business Model Teardown Challenge is an entrepreneurship and strategy competition designed to test how well you understand the businesses shaping today's economy.

From Zomato and Blinkit to CRED, Nykaa, boAt and Meesho, participants will go beyond simply studying successful companies.

You will tear down their business models, identify opportunities and vulnerabilities, and create a better way forward.

This is not just a case competition.

It is a test of how you think like an entrepreneur.

The Challenge

Every successful company has a business model.

But every business model has a weakness.

Your mission is to:

DECODE → TEAR DOWN → IDENTIFY → REBUILD → DEFEND

Understand how the business works.
Find the crack in the model.
Identify an opportunity.
Build a better business model.
Defend your idea against the jury.

Who Can Participate?

  • Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students.
  • Students from any academic discipline or specialization can participate.
  • Participants can register individually or as a team.
  • No prior entrepreneurship experience is required.

Team Size

1–3 members per team

Competition Structure

The competition consists of 3 rounds, and every round is an elimination round.

Only the teams that clear one round will move to the next.

Round 1 — the Entrepreneurial Iq

Online Quiz | Elimination Round

Think fast. Think commercially.

The first round will test your understanding of entrepreneurship, business models, startups, strategy, marketing, finance and the business ecosystem.

Topics may include:

  • Entrepreneurship & startups
  • Business models
  • Revenue models
  • Unit economics
  • Marketing & GTM
  • Startup funding
  • Business strategy
  • Famous startups & companies
  • Innovation
  • Current business trends

Format: Online Quiz
Mode: Online
Questions: 25 MCQ-based Questions
Time: 10 Minutes 
Nature: Elimination

Only the top-performing participants/teams will qualify for Round 2.

Round 2 — Tear It Down

  • Business Model Analysis & Submission | Elimination Round
  • This is where the real teardown begins.
  • Shortlisted teams will be provided with a company/business model to analyse.
  • Your task is to go beyond describing the company.
  • You need to understand why the business works, where it struggles and how you would rebuild it.

Your analysis should cover:

1. Understand the Business

  • Who is the customer?
  • What problem does the company solve?
  • What is its value proposition?
  • How does it acquire customers?
  • How does it make money?

2. Break Down the Economics

  • Revenue streams
  • Cost structure
  • Customer acquisition
  • Unit economics
  • Profitability
  • Scalability

3. Identify the Crack
Find one major weakness, risk or untapped opportunity in the existing business model.

Ask yourself:

"Where can this business model become vulnerable?"

4. Rebuild the Model

Now think like the founder.

Propose a redesigned business model that can improve the company's:

  • Revenue
  • Profitability
  • Customer acquisition
  • Retention
  • Scalability
  • Competitive advantage

5. Defend Your Idea

Your solution should not only be innovative.

It should be realistic, commercially viable and scalable.

Submission Format

  • One Slide Submission
  • PDF format
  • Original work only
  • Clear assumptions and supporting data should be mentioned
  • Submission must be made through the Unstop platform within the specified deadline

Nature: Elimination Round

Only shortlisted teams will qualify for the final round.

Round 3 — the Founder's Room

  • Online Presentation | Final Elimination Round
  • You've torn down the business.
  • You've rebuilt it.
  • Now convince the jury that your version is better.
  • Shortlisted teams will present their Business Model Teardown to a panel of judges.

Presentation Structure

5 Minutes — Presentation

Present:

  • Existing business model
  • Key insight
  • Major weakness/opportunity
  • Your redesigned model
  • Why it will work
  • Expected impact

Followed by:

3 Minutes — Jury Q&A

The jury may challenge your:

  • Assumptions
  • Business model
  • Market opportunity
  • Revenue model
  • Scalability
  • Feasibility
  • Competitive advantage

Think on your feet. Defend your business.

Judging Criteria

Participants will be evaluated on:

Criteria Weightage
Understanding of Existing Business Model 15%
Depth of Analysis 20%
Identification of Key Opportunity/Problem 20%
Innovation of Proposed Model 20%
Feasibility & Commercial Viability 15%
Scalability & Competitive Advantage 10%
Total 100%

For the final presentation, additional consideration will be given to:

  • Storytelling
  • Presentation quality
  • Clarity of thought
  • Response to jury questions
  • Ability to defend assumptions

Rules & Regulations

  • Each team can have a maximum of 3 members.
  • Participants must complete registration before the specified deadline.
  • Every round is an elimination round.
  • Only shortlisted teams from each round will progress further.
  • All submissions must be original and created by the participating team.
  • Plagiarism or submission of previously published work may result in immediate disqualification.
  • Participants must adhere to the specified submission format and deadlines.
  • Late submissions may not be considered.
  • The decision of the organizing committee and jury will be final and binding.
  • The organizers reserve the right to modify the competition schedule, format or rules if required.
  • Participants are expected to maintain professional conduct throughout the competition.
  • Any attempt to manipulate, impersonate or unfairly influence the competition process may result in disqualification.

details.title: Round 2: Tear It Down — One-Slide Submission
details.display_text:
Shortlisted teams will be given a company/business model to analyse and rebuild in one slide.

The slide should cover:

  • Business Model: How does the company create and capture value?
  • The Crack: Identify one key weakness, risk, or opportunity.
  • The Rebuild: Suggest an improved business model.
  • Why It Works: Explain the impact, scalability, and competitive advantage.

Submission Guidelines:

  • Submit exactly 1 slide in PDF format.
  • Keep it concise, visual, and data-driven.
  • Mention sources for any external data used.
  • Only original work will be accepted.
  • Submit through Unstop before the deadline.
  • This is an elimination round.

One slide. One crack. One better model.
